correctness.rationale: The normalized SAG scalar conditional moments follow by averaging the replaced table entry. Direct symbolic expansion proves a positive-definite energy with exact drift (s-2)x² for all n≥2, yielding summability below s=2 and a conserved nonzero expected energy at s=2. For s>2, det(I-T)=-2s(s-2)/n³<0 forces a real eigenvalue above one; four achievable deterministic initial moment vectors span all second moments, so universal mean-square convergence would contradict this eigenvalue. Orthogonal eigendecomposition extends the iff assertion to all SPD H.

value.rationale: The sharp n-independent stability ceiling for a genuinely random stale-table method is not a textbook deterministic gradient descent consequence. The exact quadratic energy supplies non-obvious cancellation of random table effects at all sample counts; the s=2 conservation and s>2 spectral obstruction fix the precise boundary. This is useful as a benchmark for finite-sum step-size proofs and bias analysis, without claiming general heterogeneous extension.
